pure-announcement.rationale: It is an academic paper abstract proposing a methodology, not a product launch, release note or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: No nearest concept (RAG, context layer, protocol lifecycle policy, OSV format) covers SDLC methodology or decision architecture for AI systems.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The claims trace to the linked arXiv paper, which describes its decision-architecture approach and an insurance-claim worked example a reader can inspect.

durability.rationale: This is self-described 'initial work' proposing that decision science could enhance agile SDLC, a single-paper framework with no demonstrated adoption, so like an unadopted convention it may never harden into something a reader relies on.

actionability.rationale: The captured note is an abstract plus arXiv page boilerplate; beyond the general suggestion to describe decisions and their architecture before automating them, it gives a builder no method concrete enough to apply.

atomicity.rationale: It carries one idea — extend agile SDLC with an explicit decision-architecture phase for AI decision-automation systems — statable in a single paragraph.
